table.name: concert
table.purpose: One row per concert event, recording its name, theme, year, and the stadium where it was held. Linked to singers via the singer_in_concert junction table and to stadiums via Stadium_ID.

Stadium_ID.name: Stadium_ID
Stadium_ID.description: Identifier of the stadium hosting the concert; foreign key to stadium.Stadium_ID (many concerts to one stadium).

Theme.name: Theme
Theme.description: Theme of the concert, typically a song title (e.g. 'Bleeding Love', 'Wide Awake') or a free-choice theme.

Year.name: Year
Year.description: Year the concert took place (2014 or 2015).

concert_ID.name: concert_ID
concert_ID.description: Primary key uniquely identifying each concert; referenced by singer_in_concert.concert_ID.

concert_Name.name: concert_Name
concert_Name.description: Name of the concert or concert stage/round (e.g. 'Auditions', 'Super bootcamp', 'Week 1').

table.name: singer
table.purpose: Directory of singers, each with one representative song, its release year, age, country, and sex; linked to concerts via singer_in_concert.

Age.name: Age
Age.description: Age of the singer in years (25–52).

Country.name: Country
Country.description: Country of origin of the singer (e.g. France, Netherlands, United States).

Is_male.name: Is_male
Is_male.description: Whether the singer is male; stored as 'T' (true) or 'F' (false).

Name.name: Name
Name.description: Full name or stage name of the singer.

Singer_ID.name: Singer_ID
Singer_ID.description: Primary key identifying each singer; referenced by singer_in_concert.Singer_ID.

Song_Name.name: Song_Name
Song_Name.description: Name of a song associated with the singer (one song per singer).

Song_release_year.name: Song_release_year
Song_release_year.description: Year the singer's song was released (1992–2016); stored as text but numeric.

table.name: singer_in_concert
table.purpose: Junction/association table linking singers to the concerts they perform in (many-to-many between singer and concert). Each row represents one singer's participation in one concert; the pair (Singer_ID, concert_ID) is the composite key.

Singer_ID.name: Singer_ID
Singer_ID.description: Identifier of the singer performing in the concert; foreign key to singer.Singer_ID (many-to-one). Together with concert_ID it identifies a performance row.

concert_ID.name: concert_ID
concert_ID.description: Identifier of the concert; foreign key to concert.concert_ID (many-to-one). Together with Singer_ID it identifies a performance row.

table.name: stadium
table.purpose: One row per stadium (Scottish football grounds), with its name, home club, capacity, and attendance statistics (lowest, average, highest). Concerts (table concert) are held at these stadiums, linked via Stadium_ID.

Average.name: Average
Average.description: Average attendance at the stadium (spectators per match). Values 552–2106, always between Lowest and Highest, consistent with attendance statistics.

Capacity.name: Capacity
Capacity.description: Maximum seating capacity of the stadium (spectators). Ranges 2,000–52,500 (Hampden Park).

Highest.name: Highest
Highest.description: Highest recorded attendance at the stadium (spectators). Always ≥ Average and ≥ Lowest.

Location.name: Location
Location.description: Despite the name, values are not places but the names of the football clubs that use the stadium (e.g. 'Ayr United', 'Queen's Park', 'Raith Rovers' — Scottish clubs). Effectively the home team / occupant of the stadium.

Lowest.name: Lowest
Lowest.description: Lowest recorded attendance at the stadium (spectators). Always ≤ Average and ≤ Highest.

Name.name: Name
Name.description: Name of the stadium (e.g. 'Hampden Park', 'Somerset Park').

Stadium_ID.name: Stadium_ID
Stadium_ID.description: Primary key of the stadium table; unique identifier for each stadium. Referenced by concert.Stadium_ID (many concerts per stadium).
